frozen_original.description_long: On January 19, 2021, President Donald Trump granted William E. Henry, also known as Ed Henry, a full and unconditional pardon. The Justice Department’s pardon instrument identifies the conviction as a violation of 18 U.S.C. § 641 in the U.S. District Court for the Middle District of Alabama, docket 2:18cr249-WKW-01. It says Henry was sentenced on May 2, 2019, to two years of probation, a $4,000 fine and a $100 special assessment. The instrument is primary evidence of the pardon and the sentence listed in the grant. It does not describe the underlying conduct, explain why Trump selected Henry for clemency, or establish any improper exchange or corrupt motive. This entry therefore records the documented clemency action without treating the pardon category as proof of corruption. The available DOJ clemency listing and pardon instrument support the date, identity, offense statute and sentence. A case record would be needed to describe the facts of the offense, and a documented statement or contemporaneous record would be needed to attribute a rationale to Trump. The title and short description are narrowed to the official action and avoid unsupported implications.
